description_en: Originally a two-storey Sattal, this belonged to the Maharjans of Tanani, whose ancestral deities, the Digudyahs, are seen in front. Situated at the north-eastern corner of Pimbahāḥ Pukhū and across from the Caṇḍeśvarī Bhajan Phalcā (LAL4217), this one-storeyeddharmaśālā(rest house) is reminiscent of aphalcā. Today (ca June 2020), it is embedded into a residential house belonging to a Śreṣṭha family. The building was commissioned by the local Rājopādhyāya Brahman clan from Pimbahāḥ.According to a local resident (Rājopādhyāya), the beams and pillars of the formerly destroyedphalcāat the northern entrance to Pimbahāḥ Pukhū (then called Pukhū Laṃ Phalcā) were reused to build thisdharmaśālāafter theGreatEarthquake of 1934 CE. In 1958, the residential house was sold and thus moved from Rājopādhyāya to Śreṣṭha ownership. The new owner wanted to privatise the building and the case was taken to court. The court decided in favour of the previous owners and their insistance that the monument remain public, thus underlining the function of thedharmaśālā.Later, someone named Mr. Kapali and his family moved in to the house under the condition that they would provide clarified butter, oil, and wicks for the recitation of religious songs in the Caṇḍeśvarī Phalcā. Today, the tenant runs a tailor shop.
monument_assessment: Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages)

historical_events.event_description: Caṇḍeśvarī Dharmaśālā, formerly aphalcā, was reconstructed with beams and pillars of the old building reused during the reconstruction process.
